body: SCOUT SECOND-READER REVIEW — bbeebf6f population reference shape. BLOCK, one concrete sibling-module seam: laws/Laws.scala still recognizes only AlignError.FingerprintMismatch in three PopulationLaws paths. The candidate now returns PopulationViewMismatch and PopulationRecallMismatch, so the different-view property, mixed-subject naming property, and wrong-recall property all evaluate false even though alignJVM/JS/Native pass. I confirmed the exact stale patterns at PopulationLaws around lines 502, 518, and 535 on the candidate tree. Add laws/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/laws/Laws.scala to the reservation/candidate and match the new typed cases, asserting subject and proof/aggregate or proof/supplied identities rather than parsing field strings; then run laws JVM/JS/Native from clean candidate. This is the referencing-module rule the chief just derived, now demonstrated as an actual behavioral red rather than a hypothetical risk. Everything else I checked is sound as the reference shape: subject-to-recall binding eliminates the independently sorted checksum collision; aggregate and receipt construction bypasses are closed for Scala consumers; public reads remain; structural equality and summary-only toString preserve intended behavior; no other production module references the reshaped public types. Public compatibility breaks (receipt apply/unapply and contentlessSubjects) are deliberate consequences of closing construction and correcting the no-units claim, not accidental drift. With the laws seam amended and green, I have no further objection.
